newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 22.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.

THE IRISH INDEPENDENT - Former Fine Gael Minister Michael Lowry was paid 105,000 sterling by businessman Ben Dunne which he did not disclose to parliament before his resignation last December, a tribunal probing payments to politicians was told. - Tyconn Ben Dunne handed three separate drafts of 70,000 pounds each to former Prime Minister Charles Haughey as part of a total 1.3 million pounds he arranged to pay him, the tribunal was told. - A huge intelligence and policing operation is under way to stop the IRA disrupting polling in the British elections. Intelligence sources say that the IRA may be about to switch tactics and attempt another bombing campaign in Britain.

THE IRISH TIMES - Former Prime Minister Charles Haughey has denied allegations that he received 1.3 million pounds for tycoon Ben dunne in a letter to the tribunal investigating payments to politicians. - Former Transport Minister Michael Lowry received 500,000 pounds in payments from Dunne in addition to the cost of rennovating his personal residence,the tribunal was told. - French President Jacques Chirac dissolvd parliament and called early elections to win support for reforms needed for economic and monetary union (EMU). -- Dublin Newsroom - 353-1-6613377
